The gameplay is built around car theft, violence, and general mayhem-making, with storylines that frequently take a back seat to the chaotic pleasures of simply tearing things up while the in-game police try to hunt you down. articles.summary: Your gut microbes work by 24-hour cycles of day and night. iLexx/iStock via Getty Images Plus How your body processes food is significantly influenced by daily rhythms tied to 24-hour light-dark cycles. Gut microbes convert dietary signals into molecules that intestinal cells use to synchronize nutrient absorption with feeding times. articles.author: Sophie Hurwitz and Rachel Santarsiero
articles.summary: Update, November 19: Acting Secretary of the Army Adam Telle has announced that the detonation will be postponed until November 23. On Friday, the US Army is scheduled to detonate roughly 11,000 pounds of lead azide, an unstable bomb-making chemical, in southeastern Iowa. The explosion will send a plume of lead-contaminated dust across a hundred-mile swath of the Midwest. Though the Army reportedly knew of the potential hazard for years, residents of the 400-person community of Middletown, who will be expected to evacuate, were given just a month’s notice of the plan to ignite 68 barrels of lead azide at the Iowa Army Ammunition Plant. But the dust plume’s potential 100-mile path extends far beyond Middletown, and the other communities in its path — as well as Iowa’s governor —only became aware of the plan on Monday, after the Army made a public announcement, according to the Washington Sun . The Iowa Environmental Council and the Sierra Club’s Iowa chapter filed a lawsuit on Thursday to halt the detonation. Army representatives told Middletown residents that the 40-year-old explosive stockpile must be detonated now because it has degraded to the point of becoming unstable to move.

Late into the night on November 3, while the lower 48 states were reeling from the blue wave crashing across the US, Mary Peltola took to the stage in a Sheraton hotel ballroom in Anchorage, Alaska , to greet her supporters. It wasn’t a victory speech as such—there would still be long days ahead before all votes could be counted across this vast Arctic state. But that didn’t prevent the Democratic Senate candidate from expressing her elation , bouncing up and down on stage, clapping her hands and clicking her fingers. Before she could speak, a volunteer shouted out from the back of the hall: “ Aarigaa! ” Peltola picked up the refrain, and threw it right back: “ Aarigaa! Can we just chant aarigaa ? Aarigaa! Aarigaa!” It was just one word. But it encapsulated something special about Peltola and her insurgent’s campaign to unseat the incumbent Republican US senator, Dan Sullivan: “Aarigaa” is an Iñupiaq word that is commonly understood across Alaska’s 229 federally recognized tribes. The win amplifies their voice on tribal sovereignty and subsistence rights after decades of neglect and discrimination — much as Mississippi Delta Black voters powered Democrat Scott Colom to his surprising Senate victory. The gathering in Shenzhen culminated in the first-ever trilateral meeting between the leaders of the United States, China and Russia, with nuclear arms reductions and the war in Ukraine among the issues on the table. Daily Beast journalists have been tirelessly covering the summit where Trump appeared alongside the world’s most powerful leaders, prompting mockery and embarrassment with some of his antics on the global stage. The uproar began immediately when Trump made an awkward blunder arriving in Asia. Landing first in Manila, Philippines, the 80-year-old president launched into a juvenile bit, waving a U.S. and Philippine flag in an awkward, cheerleader-like routine. Read more at The Daily Beast.
